user.title: How do your heaters connect?
user.description: Choose the cloud account if you use the TermoWeb, Ducaheat or Tevolve app. To control the heaters locally without the cloud, the easiest way is a nanoCUL USB stick plugged into this Home Assistant computer (no soldering). The ESP32 radio gateway is for advanced users: it has to be built and soldered.

menu_options.cloud: Cloud account (TermoWeb, Ducaheat or Tevolve app)
menu_options.nanocul: Local radio: nanoCUL USB stick (easiest, no soldering)
menu_options.radio: Local radio gateway: ESP32 + CC1101 (advanced, needs soldering)

cloud.title: Connect to TermoWeb family heaters
cloud.description:
Version: {version}

Choose your TermoWeb, Ducaheat, or Tevolve brand and enter your account credentials. Tevolve uses the Ducaheat backend.

radio.title: Connect to the radio gateway
radio.description: Home Assistant normally finds the ESP32 radio gateway by itself: look for it under **Discovered** on the Devices & Services page. Use this form only if it does not show up there. Enter the IP address of your gateway. In the next step you choose: add the gateway and let it find your heaters, or pair new heaters.

advanced.name: Advanced settings
advanced.description: Leave these as they are unless you changed the gateway firmware.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Radio gateway found
zeroconf_confirm.description:
Found a TermoWeb radio gateway at {host}. Set it up?

In the next step you choose: add the gateway (it finds and pairs your heaters), or only listen.

radio_method.title: Add your gateway
radio_method.description:
Choose "Add the gateway" to control your heaters. Setup finishes at once. Then:

- Heaters that already work with a TermoWeb gateway or app are found by themselves, usually within a few minutes. Heaters talk when they start heating, so turning one heater's temperature up helps.
- New or reset heaters: put each heater into pairing mode within 30 minutes. The heater's manual tells you which buttons to press. Do one heater at a time. Later, press **Pair new heaters** on the gateway device first.

You get a notification for each heater that is added.

Choose "Listen only" to record radio traffic for a test, next to a TermoWeb gateway that still runs. The integration never transmits in this mode and adds no heaters.

menu_options.radio_monitor: Listen only (record radio traffic, never transmit)

reconfigure_radio.title: Change the radio gateway
reconfigure_radio.description: Change the gateway address. Tick "Scan for heaters again" if you added or removed a heater.

nanocul.title: Connect to the nanoCUL USB stick
nanocul.description: Choose the port of your nanoCUL stick. If Home Assistant recognised the stick, it is already selected: just press Submit. In the next step you choose: add the gateway and let it find your heaters, or pair new heaters.

nanocul_manual.title: Enter the nanoCUL port
nanocul_manual.description: Type the port path, for example /dev/serial/by-id/usb-..., or a network address such as socket://192.0.2.10:2323 for a stick shared over the network.

reconfigure_nanocul.title: Change the nanoCUL port
reconfigure_nanocul.description: Change the stick's port path or URL. Tick "Scan for heaters again" if you added or removed a heater.

reconfigure.title: Change the account settings
reconfigure.description:
Version: {version}

Enter the new password for this account. You cannot switch to a different account here: add a new entry for that.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: {brand} did not accept the saved password for {username}. Enter the current password.

error.invalid_auth: Invalid username or password (or client key).
error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to TermoWeb — network/DNS/SSL error.
error.rate_limited: Temporarily rate-limited by API. Try again later.
error.cannot_connect_radio: Cannot connect to the radio gateway. Check the IP address and port, and that the gateway is powered on.
error.no_gateway_mac: The radio gateway did not report its MAC address. Update the gateway firmware.
error.no_heaters: No heater answered. Move the gateway closer to the heaters and try again.
error.cannot_connect_nanocul: Cannot open the nanoCUL stick. Check that it is plugged in, that the port is right, and that it runs the termoweb_rx firmware.

progress.radio_rescan: Checking every heater on your radio network. This takes up to a minute.

abort.already_configured: This gateway is already set up.
abort.monitor_reconfigure: A listen-only entry cannot be changed. Delete it and add it again.
abort.unique_id_mismatch: This is a different account or device. To use it, add a new entry instead.
abort.cannot_connect_radio: Cannot connect to the radio gateway. Check that the gateway is powered on and on your network.
abort.no_gateway_mac: The radio gateway did not report its MAC address. Update the gateway firmware.
abort.not_ipv4_address: The radio gateway announced only an IPv6 address. Add it by hand with its IPv4 address.
abort.nanocul_firmware_too_old: The firmware on this nanoCUL stick is too old. Put the newest termoweb_rx firmware on the stick (see the nanoCUL guide), then try again.

rehome.title: Move heaters to this installation's own network
rehome.description:
Use this when your heaters still use the radio network of an old TermoWeb gateway. Heaters: {heaters}.

What happens:
1. Each heater is reset to factory settings. Home Assistant saves its settings first.
2. You put the heaters into pairing mode, one at a time. The heater's manual tells you which buttons to press. Wait about 10 seconds between heaters. You have 5 minutes.
3. The heaters get new numbers, from 2 upwards. Their entity ids change. Heater names stay the same when Home Assistant recognises the heater.
4. Home Assistant gives each heater its settings back: mode, preset temperatures, manual temperature and weekly program.

Heater control pauses while this runs. Only dialect-B heaters can be moved. Press **Submit** to start, then put the first heater into pairing mode after about 10 seconds.

abort.not_loaded: The integration is not running. Start it first, then try again.

progress.rehome: Resetting the heaters, then waiting for heaters in pairing mode. Put one heater into pairing mode now, then the next one. This stops 1 minute after the last heater was paired, or after 5 minutes.

set_acm_preset.name: Configure accumulator boost preset
set_acm_preset.description: Update the default boost duration and/or temperature for a TermoWeb accumulator. Minutes must be between 60 and 600 in 60-minute increments; omit a field to keep the existing value.

minutes.name: Default boost duration
minutes.description: Number of minutes the boost should run when no override is provided (60–600, step 60).

temperature.name: Boost temperature
temperature.description: Optional boost setpoint to apply during the boost session (°C or °F).

start_boost.name: Start accumulator boost
start_boost.description: Trigger an immediate boost on a TermoWeb accumulator. Provide a duration to override the default (60–600 minutes in 60-minute increments), or omit it to use the stored preset.

minutes.name: Boost duration
minutes.description: Duration of the boost session in minutes (60–600, step 60). Optional.

cancel_boost.name: Cancel accumulator boost
cancel_boost.description: Cancel the active boost session on a TermoWeb accumulator.

set_schedule.name: Set weekly schedule
set_schedule.description: Set the 7×24 weekly program for a TermoWeb heater. The program is a list of 168 integers, where each value corresponds to one hour of the week starting Monday 00:00. Use 0 for the cold preset, 1 for the night preset and 2 for the day preset.

prog.name: Program
prog.description: A list of 168 integers (0, 1 or 2) representing the heater’s weekly schedule. Index 0 is Monday 00:00, index 1 is Monday 01:00, and so on.

set_preset_temperatures.name: Set preset temperatures
set_preset_temperatures.description: Set the cold, night and day preset temperatures for a TermoWeb heater. You can either provide all three temperatures as a single list (``ptemp``) or specify each one separately (``cold``, ``night`` and ``day``). Presets you leave out keep their current value.

ptemp.name: Preset temperatures
ptemp.description: A list of three temperatures [cold, night, day] in the same units as the heater (°C or °F). If provided, this will override individual cold, night and day values.

cold.name: Cold preset
cold.description: Temperature for the cold preset (°C or °F).

night.name: Night preset
night.description: Temperature for the night preset (°C or °F).

day.name: Day preset
day.description: Temperature for the day preset (°C or °F).

import_energy_history.name: Import energy history
import_energy_history.description: Import past hourly energy use of every heater and power monitor into Home Assistant statistics (the Energy dashboard). Progress is saved: if the import stops, run it again to continue.

reset_progress.name: Reset progress
reset_progress.description: Forget saved progress and import the whole period again. Existing statistics are overwritten, not deleted.

max_history_retrieval.name: Max history days
max_history_retrieval.description: How many days back to import (1 to 3650, default 7). If you already imported fewer days, only the older days are fetched.

radio_capture.name: Radio capture
radio_capture.description: Record every radio frame the gateway or nanoCUL hears for a while and save it as a JSON file in the Home Assistant configuration folder. Use it to help find unknown commands, for example the "identify" command of the TermoWeb app. It never transmits. On a normal radio entry, heater commands wait until the capture ends.

entry_id.name: Config entry ID
entry_id.description: The radio gateway or nanoCUL config entry to use, normally the listen-only one.

seconds.name: Duration
seconds.description: How long to record, 10 to 1800 seconds.

redact.name: Hide private data
redact.description: Replace network ids and heater serial numbers in the file. Without it, the file contains your network id: share it only privately.

note.name: Note
note.description: Optional text saved in the file, for example which heater you used.
note.example: identify on the living room heater

radio_survey.name: Radio survey
radio_survey.description: Listen to all radio traffic on the heater band for a while, also traffic in dialects this integration does not know, and save a report file in the Home Assistant configuration folder. Attach the file to a GitHub issue to ask for support of a new heater dialect.

entry_id.name: Config entry ID
entry_id.description: The radio gateway or nanoCUL config entry to use.

seconds.name: Duration
seconds.description: How long to listen. Heaters send most when they start or stop heating.

radio_factory_reset.name: Radio factory reset
radio_factory_reset.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Reset one radio heater to its factory settings. The heater loses all settings, its clock, its weekly program and its radio pairing, and stops talking to Home Assistant. Its last known settings are saved first. To use the heater again, press "Pair new heaters" on the gateway device and put the heater into pairing mode. Its saved settings come back when it is recognised. Only dialect-B heaters can be reset.

entry_id.name: Config entry ID
entry_id.description: The radio gateway or nanoCUL config entry to use.

heater.name: Heater number
heater.description: The heater's radio number (the number in "Heater 6").

radio_rehome.name: Radio move heaters to own network
radio_rehome.description: Move all heaters of a radio entry onto this installation's own radio network. Each heater is reset first (its settings are saved), then you put the heaters into pairing mode one at a time. The heaters get new numbers from 2 upwards and their settings are restored. Only dialect-B heaters can be moved. Heater control pauses while this runs.

entry_id.name: Config entry ID
entry_id.description: The radio gateway or nanoCUL config entry to use.

timeout.name: Wait time
timeout.description: How long to wait for the heaters' pairing buttons.
